name: gdc-cgci-htmcp-dlbcl
alternateName: HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project - Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
description:
HIV-associated lymphoma is common where HIV is common and rare in the cohorts that define lymphoma genomics. This cohort addresses that gap directly: 70 cases with whole genome sequencing on 66, RNA sequencing on 55 and microRNA on 60, of which 34 patients are recorded as Black or African American and 18 as white.
Clinical annotation is better than the cohort size suggests. Prior treatment is recorded for 81%, ECOG performance status for 71%, treatment outcome for 46%, and named regimens including CHOP-21, COM and COP for 24%.
citeAs: CRESCENT: a deep learning framework with multi-scale attention for detecting recurrent copy number alterations.

supportedQuestions: How does the genomic landscape of HIV-associated diffuse large B-cell lymphoma differ from that of lymphoma in immunocompetent patients?
Does immune status shape the tumor transcriptome in lymphoma?
What are the outcomes of HIV-associated DLBCL treated with standard regimens?

blockingLimitations.statement: 70 cases, with individual layers covering 50 to 66, limits all subgroup analysis.
HIV status, CD4 count and antiretroviral therapy are not structured fields, despite being the cohort's organizing rationale. Stage is absent for all cases.

inappropriateUses: Comparing HIV-positive with HIV-negative lymphoma within the cohort.
